message.content:
### Quick one‑liner

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – kill by **image name** (process name).  
* `code.exe` – the executable that runs VS Code on Windows.  
* `/F` – force the termination (no graceful shutdown).

---

## How it works

1. **Open a Command Prompt** (or PowerShell) with normal user rights.  
2. Run the command above.  
3. All running instances of VS Code (`code.exe`) will be terminated immediately.

> **⚠️** Any unsaved work in VS Code will be lost. Use this only when the UI is unresponsive or you need a quick reset.

---

## If you want to see which processes are running first

```cmd
tasklist | findstr /I code.exe
```

This lists all `code.exe` instances with their PIDs.  
If you prefer to kill a specific instance:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
```

Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the number shown by `tasklist`.

---

## Killing child processes too

VS Code may spawn helper processes (e.g., extensions).  
To terminate the main process **and** any child processes:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

`/T` tells `taskkill` to terminate the specified process **and** any child processes it spawned.

---

## PowerShell alternative

If you’re using PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <PID> -Force
```

---

## Summary

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code windows |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Force‑kill VS Code **and** its child processes |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Kill a specific VS Code instance |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent |

Use the one that best fits your workflow. Happy coding!
